name: factual_operator_probe_v205
question: Does the newly implemented first-order fact operator use intermediate consequences, actual successor mixtures and retained history correctly, and where does small-sample real-trial adoption fail?
kind: bounded diagnostic mechanism experiment, not a general benchmark or formal confirmation
adoption: positive mean actual paired utility difference, zero prior mean/mass1 shrinkage; at least this declared actual trial batch; not a confidence test
initial_incumbent: first legal action, identical for all variants; thereafter each variant retains its own previously adopted policy
trial_policy: both policy snapshots frozen throughout a trial batch; per-episode history reset; live factual memory updates only after the batch; heldout evaluation never enters memory
noise: independent candidate/reference environment streams within pairs; shared initial conditions; matched environment stream indices across variants; no favorable-outcome selection
discovery_policy: fixed balanced legal-action schedule, not autonomous information seeking; same actual discovery records replayed to each variant, counted once as environment work and separately as learner exposure
full_does_not_mean_full_spec: implements fixed-scale first-order factual planning, history interface, pre-observation immediate-fact errors and real-trial adoption; no adaptive expert mixture, learned semantics, causal probability model, gradient learning or SLEEP distillation
stored_review: all episode laws/draws/returns/counts, all pre-observation targets/order/loss arithmetic, all adoption and heldout aggregates; independent kernel prediction recomputation only at rows_before 0,1,7,23,47,63,95,127,191,255 per run; not a full independent multi-step neural reconstruction
outputs: exclusive directory, all actual episode traces including unfavorable trials, all pre-observation loss records, per-cycle outcomes, independent stored metric recomputation
